name: Motion language
controls: If these graphics were alive, what laws of movement would they follow? The physics and temperament of every tween: easing curves, duration scale, stagger, holds and which movement signatures are forbidden.
question: If these graphics were alive, how would they move?
notes: Motion language is the single strongest carrier of brand personality after color. Take one layout (a headline, three cards, a logo) and change only the ease: with expo.out over 700ms everything decelerates hard into place and reads as confident, engineered, Swiss (Linear, Stripe, Vercel-style product films); with back.out(1.7) over 450ms every element overshoots and settles and the same layout turns friendly, consumer, toy-like (Duolingo, Headspace territory); with steps(4) over 250ms nothing interpolates, elements jump between positions and the layout reads raw, lo-fi, anti-design (neo-brutalist, zine, terminal). Duration scale does the second half of the work: the same expo.out at 300ms is urgent, at 1400ms it is luxurious. Terminology is informal: 'springy', 'bouncy' and 'elastic' are used interchangeably in studios; this taxonomy pins them down (elastic = overshoots past the target and oscillates; springy = damped spring, one visible overshoot then settles; bouncy = rebounds off a floor, never passing the target, like bounce.out). 'Smooth' is the most over-requested and least specific word in briefs; always resolve it to a named ease and a duration. Every option bans fade-up-slide (opacity 0 plus y 20-40px to 0 on power1.out), the default AI/template entrance. Combinations are common: a piece can be precise for UI and springy for a mascot, but pick one language per direction and treat the other as a documented exception. The contract numbers are calibrated against the ten personalities in personalities/*.json and are enforced by obey.mjs.

options.what: Continuous, gentle acceleration and deceleration with no visible snap, overshoot or stop.
options.looks: Elements glide into place and slow evenly; velocity curves are symmetrical and soft; nothing draws attention to the motion itself.
options.motion: power2.out entrances, power2.in exits, power2.inOut moves at medium durations; moderate stagger; content-level overlap so the eye never waits.
options.use: Corporate product films, B2B SaaS explainers, onboarding, UI transitions where motion must stay invisible.
options.conveys: Competence, calm reliability, polish without personality risk.
options.vs: Snappy uses sharper curves (power4/expo) and half the duration; cinematic uses the same families but twice the duration with long holds. Smooth is the safe middle, which is also why it can read generic.
options.prompt: Animate everything with medium, continuous easing: entrances power2.out over 400-600ms, exits power2.in over 240-400ms, repositioning moves power2.inOut over 600-900ms. Stagger siblings 80ms. No overshoot, no bounce, no scale-from-zero, no linear tweens. Enter with a transform other than a y-slide paired with a fade: use a clip-path inset reveal, a 4-8% scale settle (1.06 to 1) or an x-offset from a mask. Hold every arrived element at least 1000ms.

options.what: Fast response with a steep initial velocity and a very short settle, like a well-tuned native UI.
options.looks: Elements are almost instantly where they need to be; the final 10% of travel eases out briefly; transitions feel like direct manipulation.
options.motion: power4.out / expo-style decel in 120-320ms, exits even shorter, tight 40-60ms stagger, short holds.
options.use: App-store promos, SaaS feature reveals, social cutdowns, UI interaction demos, developer-tool launch films.
options.conveys: Speed, responsiveness, a product that does not make you wait.
options.vs: Springy also feels fast but overshoots its target; snappy never overshoots, it decelerates hard and stops. Kinetic punch (a pacing choice) adds oversized scale slams; snappy can be subtle.
options.prompt: Make motion snappy: entrances power4.out in 200-320ms, exits power3.in in 120-200ms, moves expo.inOut in 320-480ms. Stagger 50ms. Elements should reach 90% of their travel in the first third of the tween, then settle; no overshoot, no bounce, no blur. Use short travel distances (24-60px or 4-6% scale). Hold arrived elements at least 600ms, then cut to the next beat.

options.what: Objects overshoot past their target and oscillate back and forth several times before settling, as if attached by a rubber band.
options.looks: Visible wobble: two to four decaying oscillations around the rest position; scale and rotation jiggle; shapes may stretch on the fastest frames.
options.motion: elastic.out(1,0.4) entrances and emphasis, back.in exits, long enough (550-850ms) for the oscillations to read.
options.use: Kids and consumer apps, mascot-led explainers, playful stickers, celebratory success states, social loops.
options.conveys: Exuberance, rubbery toy energy, humor. Overused it reads as cheap or chaotic.
options.vs: Springy = a damped spring with one visible overshoot then rest (elastic.out(1,0.75) or back.out); elastic = several oscillations. Bouncy = rebounds off a surface and never passes the target (bounce.out).
options.prompt: Give motion an elastic character: entrances use elastic.out(1,0.4) over 550-850ms so each element overshoots its rest position and oscillates two to three times before settling; emphasis beats use elastic.out(1,0.5) on scale (1 to 1.15 and back) or rotation (0 to 8deg). Exits use back.in(1.4) over 200-350ms. Stagger 45ms so the wobbles ripple across siblings. Enter with scale from 0.2 or rotation, never with a fade plus y-slide. Hold 700ms minimum; never wobble more than one element group at once.

options.what: Motion that behaves like a damped physical spring: fast attack, one visible overshoot, then a quick settle.
options.looks: Elements shoot slightly past their target (5-12%) and ease back once; the overshoot is felt more than seen; interfaces feel alive but controlled.
options.motion: back.out(1.7) entrances, damped elastic.out(1,0.75) for moves and emphasis, power3.in exits, tight stagger.
options.use: Contemporary consumer product films, iOS/Android-style UI demos, illustrated product motion, friendly SaaS.
options.conveys: Tactility, friendliness, responsiveness; the UI feels physical and touchable.
options.vs: Elastic oscillates several times; springy overshoots once. Snappy decelerates to a stop without passing the target. Springs in native UI (SwiftUI, Framer Motion) are defined by stiffness/damping; in GSAP approximate them with back.out or low-oscillation elastic.
options.prompt: Use damped spring motion: entrances back.out(1.7) over 300-480ms (a 6-10% overshoot then settle), moves and emphasis elastic.out(1,0.75) over 480-720ms (one overshoot, no wobble), exits power3.in over 180-300ms. Stagger 40ms. Enter by scaling from 0.6-0.85 or translating from behind a mask, never fade plus y-slide. Follow-through: child elements (icons, labels) start 60ms after their parent card so they overshoot slightly later. Hold 650ms minimum.

options.what: Objects fall or travel to a boundary and rebound off it in decaying hops, never passing through the target.
options.looks: Drops from above that hit a baseline and hop two or three times; icons that thump onto a card; squash on each contact.
options.motion: bounce.out on y (or scale for a thump), with scaleY squash at contact frames; back.in exits; medium durations.
options.use: Kids content, games, playful stickers and emoji, badge unlocks, notification counters, mascot actions.
options.conveys: Gravity-driven fun, lightness, cartoon physics.
options.vs: Elastic passes the target and swings back; bouncy stops at the target like a floor and hops upward from it. Physics-based motion computes the bounces from gravity and restitution; bouncy stylizes them with bounce.out.
options.prompt: Make objects bounce off a floor: entrances drop from 120-300px above on y with bounce.out over 600-900ms, adding a scaleY 0.85 / scaleX 1.12 squash for 100ms at the first contact (transform-origin bottom, recovering with bounce.out). Moves use bounce.out; exits back.in(1.7) over 200-350ms, jumping up and out. Stagger 60ms so drops land one after another. Never fade plus y-slide; the element is opaque the whole fall. Hold 700ms.

options.what: Light, cheeky motion with small overshoots, tilts and secondary wiggles, playful in intent rather than in strict physics.
options.looks: Cards tilt 3-6deg as they arrive, stickers pop with a slight rotation, labels peek, cursors wiggle; motion has jokes but stays legible.
options.motion: back.out(1.7) in, back.in out, sine.inOut idle wiggles; short durations; tight stagger; occasional anticipation.
options.use: Consumer apps, community products, creator tools, illustrated SaaS explainers, social promos.
options.conveys: Approachability, warmth, a brand that does not take itself too seriously.
options.vs: Cartoonish pushes exaggeration (squash, smear frames, big anticipation); playful keeps shapes rigid and exaggeration small. Elastic is a curve; playful is a temperament that mostly uses mild back eases.
options.prompt: Make motion playful but legible: entrances back.out(1.7) over 280-450ms with a small rotation (start at -6deg, land at 0) or a scale from 0.7; exits back.in(1.7) over 160-280ms. Add one idle personality beat per scene: a 2-3deg sine.inOut wiggle yoyo or a 4px hop on a sticker or mascot. Stagger 40ms. Use anticipation (a 4% scale-down, sine.inOut over 160ms) before the hero element pops. No fade plus y-slide, no blur. Hold 600ms.

options.what: Exaggerated classical-animation physics: big anticipation, squash and stretch, smear-like speed, overshoot and snappy holds.
options.looks: Objects wind up before moving, stretch along their path at peak speed, squash on landing, and freeze in strong poses; timing is uneven on purpose.
options.motion: Anticipation tween (reverse direction, 100-200ms), fast action with stretch, strong back.out landing with squash, elastic settle on appendages.
options.use: Mascot and character animation, kids brands, game marketing, comedic explainers, sticker packs.
options.conveys: Humor, energy, character; the graphics feel like actors.
options.vs: Playful is restrained and keeps shapes rigid; cartoonish deforms shapes (squash/stretch) and exaggerates timing. Bouncy is one physics behavior; cartoonish is the full toolkit of the twelve principles pushed hard.
options.prompt: Animate with exaggerated cartoon physics: before every major move, anticipate in the opposite direction for 100-200ms (back.in(2), 10-20% of the travel); then travel fast with a stretch along the path (scaleX 1.3, scaleY 0.8 at mid-flight) and land with back.out(2.5) over 350-600ms plus a squash (scaleY 0.75, scaleX 1.2) that recovers with elastic.out(1.2,0.4). Exits back.in(2) over 200ms. Stagger 50ms. Snap into strong held poses for at least 500ms. No fades, no blur-in; objects are always solid.

options.what: Motion driven as if by motors, gears and belts: constant velocity segments with abrupt, rigid starts and stops.
options.looks: Parts slide on rails at uniform speed, rotate in fixed increments like gears, conveyor-belt loops; nothing wobbles or squashes.
options.motion: Linear (ease none) travel for entrances and exits, power1.inOut for positioning moves, sequential stagger, periodic loops.
options.use: Industrial, logistics, fintech infrastructure, developer tools, process and pipeline diagrams, manufacturing explainers.
options.conveys: Reliability, systems at work, relentless throughput.
options.vs: Robotic moves in discrete, sequenced axis-by-axis steps with pauses (a robot arm); mechanical is continuous uniform travel (a conveyor). Precise is designed deceleration (expo.out) rather than machine constancy. Linear is the ease; mechanical is the whole worldview of rails, gears and rigid parts.
options.prompt: Move everything like a machine: entrances and exits translate at constant speed (ease none) along one axis over 250-600ms, entering from behind a hard mask edge or rail; repositioning moves use power1.inOut over 400-900ms. Rotations advance in fixed 45deg or 90deg increments. Stagger 100ms in strict order, no overlap between parts of the same mechanism. No overshoot, no bounce, no blur, no opacity fades: parts are solid and rigid. Hold 700ms between machine cycles.

options.what: Designed, exact motion with strong exponential deceleration, grid-locked destinations and zero overshoot.
options.looks: Elements travel fast then decelerate hard into exact grid positions; everything aligns on arrival; hairline rules draw on; nothing extra moves.
options.motion: expo.out entrances, expo.in exits, expo.inOut moves, medium durations, even stagger, clean holds.
options.use: Premium SaaS and developer-tool launches, fintech, typography-led films, design-system showcases.
options.conveys: Confidence, intelligence, craft; the product was engineered.
options.vs: Mechanical uses constant-speed travel; robotic uses stop-start sequencing; precise uses expo curves that feel human-designed. Snappy is similar but shorter and not grid-obsessed.
options.prompt: Animate with precise, engineered easing: entrances expo.out over 450-700ms, exits expo.in over 200-300ms, moves expo.inOut over 700-1000ms. Every destination snaps to the layout grid; reveal type and panels with clip-path inset wipes or from behind masks, never fades with y-slides. Stagger 80ms in reading order. Hairlines draw with scaleX 0 to 1 from the left. No overshoot, bounce, blur or scale-pop. Hold 900ms minimum.

options.what: Sequenced, one-thing-at-a-time motion like a servo or robot arm: quick accelerate-decelerate moves separated by dead stops.
options.looks: Elements move on one axis, stop, then move on the next axis; no overlap between actions; small stops read as the machine thinking.
options.motion: power3.inOut moves with 0 overlap, strict sequencing (stagger larger than duration), micro-pauses, occasional steps() for tick motion.
options.use: AI and automation products, robotics, agentic workflow demos, technical explainers, retro sci-fi.
options.conveys: Automation, determinism, a system executing instructions.
options.vs: Mechanical is continuous constant-speed motion; robotic is stop-start and sequential. Precise overlaps actions for flow; robotic forbids overlap.
options.prompt: Move like a servo-driven robot: each element moves on one axis at a time with power3.inOut over 200-450ms, comes to a dead stop, then moves on the next axis. Never overlap two moves of the same element; separate actions with 80-150ms stops. Stagger siblings 150ms so actions queue in sequence. Entrances slide from behind a mask edge with power3.inOut; exits power3.in over 120-200ms. No overshoot, bounce, blur or opacity fades. Hold 700ms after each sequence.

options.what: Constant-speed interpolation from start to end with no acceleration or deceleration.
options.looks: Uniform travel; starts and stops are abrupt; best for marquees, tickers, rotations, scrolling credits and continuous loops.
options.motion: ease none for every tween; seamless loops; long constant pans; tickers and scrolling lists.
options.use: Tickers, marquees, loops, scrolling type, rotating badges, conveyor diagrams, deliberately raw digital aesthetics.
options.conveys: Continuity, flow of time, a digital or mechanical neutrality. Used for one-off entrances it reads as unfinished.
options.vs: Mechanical is linear plus rigid-parts logic; linear is only the velocity curve. Weightless drifts at constant speed too but in slow multi-axis space.
options.prompt: Use constant-velocity motion (ease none) for all tweens: marquees and tickers loop seamlessly by duplicating content and translating xPercent -100 over 1000-1600ms per module; entrances slide in from behind a mask edge at constant speed over 400-700ms; rotations spin at a fixed rate. Stagger 100ms. Do not add easing, overshoot, blur or scale-from-zero. Hold 800ms on key frames between loops.

options.what: Very slow, circular deceleration, long holds and stillness, where restraint itself is the signal of value.
options.looks: One element moves at a time; reveals open from the center; hairlines draw; large negative space; long stillness between beats.
options.motion: circ.out entrances over 1.4-2s, circ.in exits, power1.inOut drifts, 200ms stagger, 1.8s minimum holds.
options.use: Luxury, fashion, premium hardware, hospitality, high-end product reveals, perfume and watch brands.
options.conveys: Exclusivity, calm, confidence that does not need to shout.
options.vs: Cinematic is slow too but adds camera push, focus pulls and drama; luxurious is still and minimal. Floating is slow but loops and bobs; luxurious arrives and stops.
options.prompt: Move slowly and sparingly: entrances circ.out over 1400-2000ms using center-out clip-path reveals (inset 50% to 0) or a 1.04 to 1 scale settle; exits circ.in over 900-1400ms; any continuous drift power1.inOut. Only one element moves at a time; stagger 200ms. Hold every arrived state at least 1800ms of stillness. No overshoot, bounce, blur, scale-pop, linear tweens or fade plus slide.

options.what: Film-grammar motion: motivated push-ins, focus pulls, long eased camera moves that land, and reads during which something always keeps acting.
options.looks: Type resolves from out-of-focus to sharp, the camera pushes toward what matters and lands, dark grades, letterboxed composition, dramatic reveals.
options.motion: power2.out entrances with blur-to-sharp, power2.inOut exits, camera moves that go somewhere (4% a second or faster) and land; secondary motion under every read, never a slow drift.
options.use: Launch films, trailers, title sequences, brand manifestos, keynote openers.
options.conveys: Drama, significance, a premium event.
options.vs: Luxurious/slow keeps one slow mover between moves; cinematic moves its camera with intent between reads. Smooth has similar curves but short durations and no camera language.
options.prompt: Use film grammar: entrances resolve from blur(16-24px) and scale 1.08 to sharp at scale 1 with power2.out over 1100-1600ms; exits dissolve back to blur with power2.inOut over 700-1100ms. Under every read keep secondary motion going (a line's slow carry, a rack of focus, the next element arriving) so the frame never freezes; when the camera moves it goes somewhere (scale 1 to 1.12 over 1200-1800ms, power2.inOut), never a slow push (under 4% a second is a creep). Stagger 160ms. No overshoot, bounce, scale-pop, linear tweens or fade plus y-slide. Hold 1400ms minimum.

options.what: Motion that follows living, growing systems: soft sine curves, arcs rather than straight lines, uneven timing and growth from a source.
options.looks: Shapes grow like plants from a root, paths curve, siblings arrive with irregular offsets, blobs breathe; nothing moves on a straight rail.
options.motion: sine.out growth, sine.in retreat, sine.inOut breathing loops; motion along curved paths; irregular stagger.
options.use: Health, wellness, sustainability, food, biotech, calm consumer brands.
options.conveys: Life, growth, warmth, naturalness.
options.vs: Fluid is about continuous flow between states; organic is about growth and irregularity. Floating is buoyancy in place; organic grows and spreads.
options.prompt: Make motion organic: grow elements from a source point (scale from transform-origin at their root, or strokes drawing from the base) with sine.out over 1000-1500ms; retreat with sine.in; idle states breathe with a 2-3% sine.inOut scale yoyo over 2200ms. Move along curved arcs, never straight lines. Stagger around 90ms with plus/minus 30ms irregularity. No bounce, no scale-from-zero pops, no linear tweens, no fade plus slide. Hold 1100ms.

options.what: Uninterrupted flow in which every state change hands off into the next, with no visible stops or cuts between elements.
options.looks: One shape becomes the next, panels slide into and out of each other, motion paths chain; the eye is carried continuously.
options.motion: power3.inOut state changes with overlapping tweens, sine.inOut connective drift, tight stagger, shared-element handoffs.
options.use: Product films built as one continuous take, UI walkthroughs, brand identity systems, premium explainers.
options.conveys: Seamlessness, integration, ease of use.
options.vs: Liquid simulates the material behavior of liquid (ripples, blobs, surface tension); fluid only describes continuity of motion and can apply to rigid cards. Smooth concerns the curve; fluid concerns the handoffs between moves.
options.prompt: Keep motion fluid and continuous: every state change uses power3.inOut over 500-1200ms and starts 30-40% before the previous tween ends so there is never a dead frame. Hand elements off by transforming the outgoing element into the incoming one (shared-element position/size tweens, clip-path morphs) instead of exit-then-enter. Connective drift sine.inOut. Stagger 40ms. No bounce, scale-pop, linear tweens, opacity-only entrances or fade plus slide. Hold 900ms.

options.what: Graphics behave like a liquid material: they pour, pool, ripple, merge into blobs and drain away.
options.looks: Letters pour up from a baseline, shapes merge with gooey bridges, surfaces ripple, edges wobble with a travelling wave.
options.motion: power4.inOut pours and drains with skew relaxing to 0, tight 30ms stagger so a line flows, sine.inOut ripple waves during holds.
options.use: Beverage and beauty brands, creative tools, music, experimental brand motion, gradient-heavy identities.
options.conveys: Sensuality, transformation, hypnotic flow.
options.vs: Fluid is continuity of rigid elements; liquid is deformation of the material itself. Elastic stretches and snaps back; liquid does not snap, it flows and settles.
options.prompt: Make graphics behave like liquid: characters and shapes pour up from a baseline (scaleY 0 to 1, transform-origin bottom, skewX 12deg relaxing to 0) with power4.inOut over 800-1200ms, staggered 30ms so the line flows; drain back the same way on exit. During holds, pass a slow sine.inOut wave through elements (y plus/minus 4px, stagger 30ms, yoyo). For merging shapes use an SVG gooey filter (feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 10 plus feColorMatrix alpha threshold). No bounce, blur-in, linear tweens or fade plus slide. Hold 800ms.

options.what: Elements hover and bob gently around a rest point, as if suspended in water or air.
options.looks: Cards and 3D objects rise and sink a few pixels on slow loops, slight rotation sway, offset phases so nothing moves in unison.
options.motion: sine.out arrivals, sine.inOut yoyo bobbing (4-12px, 1.8-2.6s), phase-offset loops, long holds.
options.use: Landing-page heroes, spatial UI, 3D product showcases, ambient loops, wellness brands.
options.conveys: Lightness, calm, a dreamlike suspension.
options.vs: Weightless has no rest point: objects drift and rotate indefinitely in zero gravity. Floating always returns to its rest position.
options.prompt: Float every element around a rest point: arrive with sine.out over 1200-1800ms (a 20-40px travel from behind a mask or a 1.05 to 1 scale settle), then bob on y by 6-12px with sine.inOut yoyo repeat over 1800-2600ms and sway rotation plus/minus 1.5deg; offset each element's phase by 300-600ms so nothing bobs in unison. Exits sine.in. Stagger 70ms. No bounce, overshoot, scale-pop, linear tweens or fade plus slide. Hold 1500ms.

options.what: Zero-gravity motion: objects drift at constant slow velocity and keep rotating, with no floor, no settling and no rest point.
options.looks: Objects tumble slowly on multiple axes, drift across the frame and past each other, never quite stop.
options.motion: power1.out arrival, then constant-velocity (ease none) drift and rotation over long durations; very long holds.
options.use: Space and deep-tech themes, abstract brand films, 3D object showcases, ambient backgrounds, AI imagery.
options.conveys: Awe, vastness, freedom from friction, the future.
options.vs: Floating bobs around a fixed rest point; weightless keeps drifting. Inertial carries momentum then decelerates to rest; weightless never decelerates.
options.prompt: Animate in zero gravity: elements arrive with power1.out over 1000-1600ms and then drift at constant velocity (ease none) 40-120px and rotate 10-30deg across 2400-3600ms, on slightly different vectors so objects pass each other. Nothing settles, bobs back or bounces. Exits power1.in drifting out of frame. Stagger 120ms. No bounce, overshoot, scale-pop, linear entrances or fade plus slide. Hold 1600ms.

options.what: Motion that communicates large mass: slow to start, accelerating under gravity, landing with impact and minimal rebound.
options.looks: Blocks drop and slam, the frame shakes on impact, dust or a shockwave line appears, then everything stays put.
options.motion: power4.in drops ending on impact, a 2-4 frame camera shake, power3.inOut for slow pushes, no overshoot.
options.use: Bold announcements, sports, hardware, infrastructure, security, brutalist and industrial brands.
options.conveys: Solidity, power, permanence, seriousness.
options.vs: Bouncy rebounds after impact; heavy absorbs it. Kinetic punch slams type in with fast decel (power4.out); heavy accelerates into the impact (power4.in) because gravity does the work.
options.prompt: Give everything mass: entrances accelerate into place with power4.in over 450ms (falling from 150-300px or pushing in from a mask edge) and end on an impact; on impact shake the parent container 6-10px with one 120ms power3.inOut x tween (yoyo, repeat 1) and flash a 1px shockwave line. Heavy moves use power3.inOut over 800-1200ms, slow to start and slow to stop; exits power3.in over 250ms. Stagger 120ms so each impact is felt separately. No overshoot, bounce, scale-pop, blur or fades. Hold 900ms.

options.what: Motion that obeys a consistent physical model: gravity arcs, collisions, restitution and friction applied the same way to every object.
options.looks: Objects follow parabolic arcs, fall and collide, stack, roll and come to rest according to believable rules.
options.motion: Rising on power2.out and falling on power2.in (parabolas), bounce.out for collisions, friction decel, consistent gravity across objects.
options.use: Playful product demos (items dropping into carts, blocks stacking), games, data 'pile-up' charts, toy-like 3D.
options.conveys: Believability, tangibility, satisfying cause and effect.
options.vs: Bouncy is a stylized ease; physics-based keeps one gravity constant and derives every bounce from it. Inertial covers momentum only, not gravity or collisions.
options.prompt: Apply one consistent physical model: throws rise on y with power2.out and fall with power2.in while a single power2.out x tween spans the whole flight, giving near-parabolic arcs; collisions with the floor use bounce.out over 550-800ms with each rebound under half the previous height; sliding objects decelerate with power2.out to a friction stop. Use the same gravity (fall durations proportional to the square root of height) for every object. Stagger 60ms. No fade plus slide, no scale-pop, no blur, no linear entrances. Hold 700ms after objects come to rest.

options.what: Objects keep moving after the force that started them stops, gliding on a long decelerating tail until friction brings them to rest.
options.looks: Flicked cards glide and slowly settle, carousels coast, scroll-like momentum, long tails at the end of every move.
options.motion: expo.out entrances and power3.out moves with long durations so the tail is visible; power3.in exits; no spring-back.
options.use: Mobile UI demos (scroll, swipe, flick), carousels, card stacks, product tours of touch interfaces.
options.conveys: Tactile realism, responsiveness to touch, a product that feels natural in the hand.
options.vs: Springy returns past the target; inertial glides to a stop without returning. Weightless never stops; inertial always stops.
options.prompt: Drive motion by momentum: each move starts at full speed as if flicked and decelerates over a long tail: entrances expo.out over 800-1200ms, moves power3.out over 800-1700ms, covering large distances (200-600px) so the glide reads. Exits power3.in over 300-500ms. Nothing springs back or overshoots. Stagger 60ms. No bounce, scale-pop, blur, linear entrances or fade plus slide. Hold 900ms.

options.what: Motion that traces the energy of a hand gesture: sweeping arcs, a fast attack and a dragging finish, like a brush or a flick of the wrist.
options.looks: Strokes swoosh on along curved paths, elements travel in arcs with a thick-to-thin speed profile, trailing lines follow the gesture.
options.motion: power3.out swooshes along motion paths, strokes drawn with stroke-dashoffset, power2.in exits, arcs everywhere.
options.use: Handwritten and signature reveals, editorial and fashion, illustrated explainers, sports and energy brands.
options.conveys: Human energy, spontaneity, confidence of the hand.
options.vs: Handmade/imperfect jitters and boils frame to frame; gestural is smooth but expressive and arced. Organic grows from a source; gestural sweeps from a flick.
options.prompt: Animate with the energy of a hand gesture: elements travel along curved arcs (GSAP MotionPathPlugin or combined x/y tweens with different eases) with power3.out over 300-800ms, fast at the start and dragging into the finish; strokes draw on via stroke-dashoffset with power3.out, trailing a thinner echo line 60ms behind. Exits sweep off with power2.in along a continuation of the same arc. Stagger 70ms. No straight-line slides, no fades with slides, no blur, no linear entrances. Hold 800ms.

options.what: Deliberately imperfect motion with frame-to-frame jitter (line boil), uneven spacing and slightly irregular timing, as if drawn by hand.
options.looks: Outlines wobble on a 3-frame boil, items arrive at slightly different speeds and angles, wobbly rotation, nothing is pixel-perfect.
options.motion: power2.out entrances with randomized small rotations and offsets, a stepped boil loop (steps(3)) on outlines, irregular stagger.
options.use: Doodle and hand-drawn UI explainers, illustrated product motion, craft and indie brands, education.
options.conveys: Warmth, humanity, approachability; the opposite of corporate polish.
options.vs: Stop-motion-like drops the frame rate for everything; handmade keeps motion smooth but adds boil and irregularity. Gestural is expressive but clean.
options.prompt: Make motion feel hand-made: entrances power2.out over 280-700ms with a random 2-5deg starting rotation and 4-10px offsets that settle to near (not exactly) zero; exits power2.in. Give outlines a line boil: loop through 3 slightly different path variants or SVG feTurbulence seeds with steps(3) over 250ms, repeat infinite. Stagger around 90ms with plus/minus 30ms randomness (seeded, deterministic). No fade plus slide, blur, linear entrances or opacity-only entrances. Hold 800ms.

options.what: Motion rendered at a reduced frame rate (12 fps, on twos) so objects jump between held poses like physical stop-motion or hand-drawn animation.
options.looks: Paper cutouts and objects move in visible discrete steps; slight position noise per frame; tactile, crafted.
options.motion: steps(N) eases matched to 12fps (N = duration in ms / 83), small per-frame jitter, no smooth interpolation.
options.use: Paper-cut and collage explainers, craft brands, music videos, social content wanting a tactile feel.
options.conveys: Craft, nostalgia, tangibility, charm.
options.vs: Choppy/stepped uses very few steps as a graphic attitude (brutalist); stop-motion-like keeps full choreography but samples it at 12fps. Handmade keeps smooth frame rate.
options.prompt: Render motion as if shot at 12fps: every tween uses steps(N) where N is duration divided by 83ms (e.g. 500ms uses steps(6)); entrances steps(6), exits steps(4), moves steps(12) over durations of 167, 250, 417, 667 and 1000ms. Add 1-2px per-step position jitter and a 0.5deg rotation wobble. Stagger 83ms (one frame at 12fps). No smooth fades, fade plus slide, blur or opacity-only entrances. Hold 750ms.

options.what: No interpolation as an aesthetic: elements jump between a few discrete positions or cut instantly.
options.looks: Words and panels snap between 3-6 positions, mis-registration, inversion flashes, hard cuts; loud and raw.
options.motion: steps(3-6) eases, zero-duration set() cuts, jitter, instant exits.
options.use: Neo-brutalist brands, zines, fashion and music promos, anti-design social content.
options.conveys: Rawness, rebellion, urgency, anti-polish.
options.vs: Stop-motion-like keeps a full move sampled at 12fps; choppy uses a handful of steps as a graphic attitude. Glitchy adds digital corruption (slices, RGB split).
options.prompt: Nothing interpolates: use steps(4) for entrances, steps(3) for exits, steps(6) for moves over 100-600ms, or zero-duration tl.set() cuts on the timeline. Words appear offset in x on stepped jitters then snap to place; invert ink and background for 2-3 frames on beats. Stagger 60ms. No fades, fade plus slide, blur, bounce or overshoot. Hold 500ms.

options.what: Motion that simulates digital failure: horizontal slice offsets, RGB channel splits, flicker and frame skips.
options.looks: Elements tear into horizontal bands that offset, color channels separate, brief flickers and pixel blocks, then snap clean.
options.motion: Very short stepped tweens (60-250ms), clip-path slice offsets, x jitter, text scramble, clean resolve.
options.use: Cybersecurity, gaming, crypto, music, tech launches with an edge, error or hack story beats.
options.conveys: Instability, digital rawness, disruption, hacker energy.
options.vs: Choppy/stepped is clean discrete motion; glitchy adds corruption artifacts. Chaotic is many uncoordinated elements; glitchy is one element failing.
options.prompt: Animate like a failing signal: entrances build from 3-5 horizontal clip-path slices offset 10-40px in x that snap to 0 with steps(5) over 160-250ms; duplicate the element in red and cyan (mix-blend-mode screen) offset 3-6px for 2-3 frames; flicker opacity on steps(3). Moves steps(8) jitter; exits tear out with steps(3) in 60-100ms. Stagger 30ms. Always resolve to a clean, legible state. No blur, bounce, overshoot, scale-pop or fade plus slide. Hold 600ms.

options.what: Many elements moving at once in varied directions, speeds and scales, deliberately overwhelming before resolving.
options.looks: Dense overlapping type and stickers flying from every edge, rotations, collisions, then a sudden snap to one clear message.
options.motion: power4.out slams and expo moves at very short durations, randomized directions and 20ms stagger, sudden resolution.
options.use: Social promos, youth and streetwear brands, festival and event openers, music, hype reels.
options.conveys: Overload, excitement, noise of culture; the resolution becomes the payoff.
options.vs: Generative variety comes from rules and seeds and often feels calm; chaotic is choreographed overload. Glitchy is corruption of one element.
options.prompt: Choreograph controlled chaos: 12-40 elements enter from random edges and angles (seeded random: x plus/minus 800px, rotation plus/minus 45deg, scale 0.5-2) with power4.out over 150-400ms, stagger 20ms from random; secondary moves expo.inOut; everything overlaps. After 1.5-3s snap every element away (power4.in, 80-150ms) and resolve to one clean message held 350ms or more. No fade plus slide, no blur-in, no opacity-only entrances.

options.what: Motion and form produced by a system of rules with seeded randomness, so the composition emerges rather than being hand-placed.
options.looks: Fields of dots, lines or glyphs arranged by noise or rules, each element subtly different, patterns that evolve and recombine.
options.motion: Many small elements animated with the same ease but randomized (seeded) delays, amplitudes and directions; slow evolution.
options.use: Brand identity systems, AI and data companies, ambient backgrounds, event visuals, music visualizers.
options.conveys: Intelligence, complexity, living systems, infinite variation.
options.vs: Procedural motion is computed from formulas and may be fully deterministic without randomness; generative adds seeded randomness to produce the composition itself. Chaotic is hand-choreographed overload.
options.prompt: Build the scene as a generative system: generate 100-600 small elements (dots, dashes, glyphs) from a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 with a fixed seed so renders are deterministic), placed by a rule (grid with noise jitter, Poisson disk or flow field). Animate them with power2.out entrances over 500-1200ms using gsap stagger {each: 0.025, from: 'random'}, then evolve positions or sizes with sine.inOut over 1200-2000ms. Exits power2.in. No fade plus slide, bounce, overshoot or blur. Hold 1000ms on resolved patterns.

options.what: Motion computed from formulas and parameters (index, distance, sine, noise) rather than hand-set keyframes.
options.looks: Ripples spreading through grids by distance from a point, wave patterns through rows of bars, clockwork-perfect repetition.
options.motion: Stagger functions from center or edges, per-element values derived from index or distance, sine-driven oscillation, deterministic loops.
options.use: Data and infrastructure brands, grid-based identities, loading states, technical explainers, loops.
options.conveys: Order, systems thinking, mathematical beauty.
options.vs: Generative uses seeded randomness to create variation; procedural can be fully deterministic and regular. Rhythmic is timed to a meter; procedural is timed by formula.
options.prompt: Derive motion from formulas: lay out a grid or row of 20-200 elements and animate with gsap stagger {each: 0.03, grid: 'auto', from: 'center'} so a wave spreads by distance; per-element amplitude = base times sin(index times 0.4) or distance falloff. Entrances power3.out over 400-900ms, exits power3.in, oscillations sine.inOut yoyo repeat. No keyframe hand-tweaks, no randomness unless seeded. No fade plus slide, bounce, overshoot or blur. Hold 900ms.

options.what: Motion organized on a regular meter so entrances, pulses and holds repeat at fixed musical intervals, with or without a soundtrack.
options.looks: Elements arrive on a steady count, pulses repeat, patterns of short-short-long; the viewer can tap along.
options.motion: Durations and delays that are fractions of one beat (e.g. 500ms at 120 BPM), power3.out hits, sine.inOut pulses.
options.use: Kinetic typography, social promos, lists and feature montages, loops, brand idents.
options.conveys: Momentum, confidence, musicality.
options.vs: Beat-synchronized locks to an actual audio track's transients; rhythmic only follows an internal meter. Staccato (pacing) is about short beats; rhythmic is about regular ones.
options.prompt: Place every event on a 120 BPM grid (one beat = 500ms): entrances power3.out lasting 250 or 500ms and starting exactly on beats or eighths (250ms), exits power3.in on the offbeat, pulses sine.inOut scale 1 to 1.04 lasting one beat. Use a repeating pattern (hit, hit, hold) across scenes. Stagger 125ms (a sixteenth). No fade plus slide, blur, bounce or linear entrances. Hold 1000ms (two beats).

options.what: Motion locked to the transients of a specific music track so impacts, cuts and pulses land exactly on kicks, snares and drops.
options.looks: Words slam on every kick, scenes cut on snares, a zoom punch on the drop; visuals feel like the music made them.
options.motion: Durations as note values at the track's BPM, power4.out slams that complete on the transient, expo.out camera punches on drops.
options.use: Social ads, trailers, event openers, music-led product reels, hype videos.
options.conveys: Energy, momentum, a tight audio-visual unity.
options.vs: Rhythmic follows an internal meter; beat-synchronized follows a real audio file's beat map. Speech-synchronized follows words, not music.
options.prompt: Lock motion to the track: detect BPM and beat times from the audio (for the default 128 BPM, one beat = 469ms). Durations are note values: 117, 234, 469, 938, 1875ms. Every entrance uses power4.out and starts so the element lands on its beat; scene cuts land on snares; the drop gets an expo.out scale punch (1.15 to 1). Stagger by an eighth note (234ms). No fade plus slide, blur, bounce, linear or opacity-only entrances. Hold two beats (938ms) minimum.

options.what: Motion timed to spoken words so text, highlights and visuals appear exactly as the voiceover says them.
options.looks: Each word or key phrase appears on its spoken timestamp, emphasis words get a color or scale hit, visuals change on sentence boundaries.
options.motion: power3.out word entrances placed at transcript timestamps, power2.in exits at phrase ends, power2.inOut scene moves on sentence breaks.
options.use: Explainers, captioned social video, tutorials, talking-head graphics, narrated product films.
options.conveys: Clarity, accessibility, authority; the graphics and voice say one thing together.
options.vs: Beat-synchronized follows music transients; speech-synchronized follows word timestamps. Stagger is not fixed: words land when they are spoken.
options.prompt: Time motion to the voiceover transcript: each word or key phrase enters at its word-level timestamp with power3.out over 120-320ms (a mask rise or a color-fill highlight, never fade plus slide); emphasized words get a 1.08 scale or accent color on the stressed syllable; phrase-end exits power2.in; scene changes use power2.inOut on sentence boundaries. The nominal stagger is 400ms (about 150 words per minute) but real timestamps override it. No bounce, blur-in or linear entrances. Hold each phrase at least 600ms after its last word.

options.what: Motion starts slowly and accelerates, ending at full speed.
options.prompt: Use an ease-in curve (power2.in to power4.in, expo.in) for exits and for objects leaving under gravity; never for arrivals, which would slam at full speed without deceleration.

options.what: Motion starts at full speed and decelerates into its resting position.
options.prompt: Use ease-out (power3.out, expo.out, circ.out) for entrances: elements should cover most of their travel in the first third of the tween and settle gently into the final position.

options.what: Motion accelerates from rest and decelerates back to rest, an S-shaped velocity curve.
options.prompt: Use ease-in-out (power2.inOut, sine.inOut, expo.inOut) for on-screen repositioning and camera moves where the object starts and ends at rest in frame.

options.what: The object travels past its target and returns to it.
options.prompt: Add overshoot with back.out(1.4-2) so the element passes its target by 5-15% and returns; keep overshoot on entrances and emphasis, never on exits.

options.what: A small preparatory move in the opposite direction before the main action, signalling that something is about to happen.
options.prompt: Before the main move, pull the element 10-20% of the travel distance the opposite way (or scale to 0.94) over 100-200ms with power2.out, then launch the main tween immediately.

options.what: Parts of an object keep moving after the main body stops, then settle.
options.prompt: When a parent card stops, let attached parts (labels, icons, a tail, a tag) continue 4-10px or 3-6deg past rest and settle with elastic.out(1,0.6) or back.out over 300-500ms, starting 40-80ms after the parent.

options.what: Smaller movements that support the primary action without competing with it.
options.prompt: Pair each primary action with one subordinate motion at 20-40% amplitude: a shadow that scales with a lift, an icon that rotates 8deg as its button presses, a glow that pulses as a card lands.

options.what: An object compresses along the axis of impact while expanding perpendicular to it, preserving volume.
options.prompt: On impact, set scaleY 0.75-0.85 and scaleX 1.15-1.25 with transform-origin at the contact edge for 60-100ms, then recover to 1 with back.out or elastic.out.

options.what: An object elongates along its direction of travel at peak speed, preserving volume.
options.prompt: At the fastest point of a move, stretch along the travel axis (scaleX 1.2-1.4, scaleY 0.8-0.85, rotated to the direction of travel), returning to 1 as it decelerates.

options.what: Rebounds off a surface in decaying hops, never passing through the surface.
options.prompt: Use bounce.out on the y axis so the element hits its rest line and hops 2-3 times with decreasing height; add squash on the first contact.

options.what: The final small adjustments as an object comes to rest after overshoot or oscillation.
options.prompt: End energetic moves with a visible settle: a damped elastic.out(1,0.6-0.8) or a 60-120ms back.out correction so the element arrives with one or two diminishing corrections, not a dead stop.

options.what: The tendency of a moving object to keep going in proportion to its speed and mass.
options.prompt: Make faster or larger objects take longer to stop: scale deceleration time with speed (power3.out tails of 600-1200ms for flicked elements) and let a moving group carry 5-10% past its cue before slowing.

options.what: Resistance to a change in motion: objects at rest are slow to start, moving objects slow to stop.
options.prompt: Give heavy elements slow starts (power3.in or power3.inOut ramp over 300-500ms) and long stops; light elements start instantly. Heavier equals longer ramps.

options.what: Loose or trailing parts lag behind the leading part of a moving object.
options.prompt: Offset trailing parts of a moving group by 40-100ms and let them rotate 3-8deg against the direction of travel, catching up as the leader decelerates.

options.what: Motion modeled on a damped spring defined by stiffness and damping, producing overshoot and settle.
options.prompt: Approximate a spring with elastic.out(amplitude 1, period 0.4-0.8): lower period means stiffer, more oscillations; use back.out(1.7) for a critically damped single overshoot.

options.what: A fixed delay between the start times of sibling elements running the same animation.
options.prompt: Stagger siblings by a constant each value (30-200ms depending on the language) in reading order, or from center/edges/random via gsap stagger {each, from}.

options.what: A stagger that propagates spatially, like a wave or a falling row of dominoes, across a group.
options.prompt: Propagate the animation through the layout with stagger {each: 0.04, grid: 'auto', from: 'start' or 'center'} so it reads as a wave rolling across rows and columns.

options.what: Time between a trigger and the start of an animation.
options.prompt: Delay subordinate elements 100-300ms after the hero lands so the hierarchy reads: headline, then subhead, then supporting UI.

options.what: The next animation begins before the previous one ends, so motion never waits.
options.prompt: Start each following tween 20-40% before the previous ends using timeline position parameters ('-=0.2' or '<0.15') so there are no dead frames between actions.

options.what: An animation that repeats seamlessly so the last frame leads into the first.
options.prompt: Build loops with repeat: -1 and matching start/end states (yoyo for there-and-back, or duplicated content translated -100% for continuous marquees); keep loop lengths to whole multiples of the scene beat.

options.what: A period where an element stays still after arriving so it can be read.
options.prompt: Hold each arrived element for at least the language's hold_ms (and at least 300ms per 10 words of text) before exiting or moving it again.

options.what: A deliberate moment of stillness in the whole frame, used for emphasis or anticipation.
options.prompt: Insert a 400-1200ms whole-frame pause (nothing moving) immediately before the key reveal so the payoff lands harder.

options.what: Increasing speed over time; the in-part of an ease.
options.prompt: Use acceleration (ease-in families) for departures, falls and builds toward a cut; stronger power (power4, expo) means a more sudden takeoff.

options.what: Decreasing speed over time; the out-part of an ease.
options.prompt: Use deceleration (ease-out families) for arrivals and landings; expo.out decelerates hardest, sine.out softest; choose the family to set the personality.
